A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRADIEND study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original encoder correlations, decoder parameter sweeps, debiasing comparisons and GLUE/SuperGLUE evaluations in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds encoder stability, WIKIGENDER generalization and fine-tuning-order experiments.

M1.justification: The gradient-difference target, single-neuron tanh encoder, linear decoder and additive weight update remain unchanged. The new MLM multi-token paragraph documents handling without establishing a procedural change; both versions explicitly retain single-token training.

E1.justification: v4 adds WIKIGENDER evaluation using longer encyclopedic contexts and five gendered token pairs, four beyond the training pair he/she (Appendices B.7 and E.3). WSC was already included within SuperGLUE, so its new ablation does not introduce another task.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain CDA, DROPOUT, INLP, RLACE, LEACE, SENTDEBIAS, SELFDEBIAS and the same hybrid methods. The new WSC ablation varies GRADIEND placement without introducing another debiasing comparator.

E3.justification: New protocols include 1,000 WIKIGENDER examples per target and a five-model WSC ablation comparing GRADIEND before, after and both before and after fine-tuning, using accuracy, SS and SEAT. Existing splits, training budgets and benchmark protocols remain unchanged; Appendix G.2 clarifies existing averaging.

E4.justification: Appendices E.2, E.3 and H substantially extend reliability testing through cross-run encoder stability, corpus/target-shift generalization and fine-tuning-order ablations. The earlier decoder sweeps and name-based overfitting analysis are retained, with the latter moving from Appendix H to I.

E5.justification: v3 already documented three gender-training seeds and best-run selection. v4 newly reports per-run correlations, pairwise mean absolute encoding differences and distributions in Table 7 and Figure 6. No increase in run counts or change to existing bootstrap confidence-interval procedures is stated.

E6.justification: Substantial new stability, transfer and fine-tuning results reveal model-dependent failures: Table 7 includes BERT-base CorEnc of 0.076, while Table 13 reports WSC accuracy of 62.50% before versus 36.54% after applying GRADIEND to fine-tuned BERT-base. v4 also replaces the duplicated GPT-2 heatmaps and adds the missing LLaMA-Instruct Jewish/Muslim selection row. Existing comparative benchmark table scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal feature and gradient definitions, encoder-decoder equations, model-selection metrics and decoder-symmetry derivation are retained. The added proportional-rank explanation documents an existing metric rather than introducing new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, H1/H2 hypotheses, introduction's gender-debiasing state-of-the-art claim and conclusion's two central contributions retain their meaning and scope. The additional experiments do not redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: v4 interprets RoBERTa's encoder as narrowly he/she-specific, discusses alternative-token prediction spaces and single-neuron expressivity limits, and adds fine-tuning-order tradeoffs. Appendix H's description of task-performance reductions as slight understates some losses in Table 13.

D1.justification: v4 newly states dataset publication and lists eight Hugging Face identifiers in Table 4, updates the code address, and documents MLM masking, included parameter groups and summary-score aggregation. Existing hardware, hyperparameters and training-time disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds a comparison between GRADIEND's coverage across layers and typically layer-specific SAEs, citing Brinkmann et al. (2025). Additional references to Levesque et al., GPT-4o and Wikimedia support the experimental and data descriptions without substantially changing research positioning.

P1.justification: The main narrative receives localized clarifications and reference corrections. Appendices gain dataset and encoder-analysis subsections, expanded aggregation explanations and a new fine-tuning section; existing overfitting and example sections are renumbered rather than removed.

P2.justification: v4 adds Figures 6–7 and Tables 4, 7 and 13, annotates Table 2's comparability limitations and reorders selected-model rows. Figure 8(e) replaces v3 Figure 6(e), which duplicated RoBERTa's panel under GPT-2. Most existing displays retain their design and content.

improvement.justification: The new reliability and transfer analyses, dataset access information and corrected GPT-2 panel improve evidential transparency and reproducibility. The net gain is limited by Appendix H's overly broad debiasing interpretation and its description of WSC losses reaching 26.92 percentage points as slight.
